en.title: Vale and Wabtec sign agreement to enhance operational safety on the EFC and EFVM railways with advanced signaling technology
en.subtitle: Wabtec's PTC System Strengthens Vale's Rail Safety on Carajás and Vitória to Minas Lines Through 2031
en.body:
Adoption of the PTC system boosts predictability and reliability in railway operations.


       View of km 45 in Bacabeira (MA), where cargo is transported along the Carajás Railroad (EFC), operated by Vale. 
                                                                               Photo: Cristiano Oliveira

Vale is advancing its innovation and logistics efficiency strategy by adopting an advanced operational safety system for its rail transport. The company announced an agreement with Wabtec (NYSE:WAB) to implement the Positive Train Control (PTC) solution in railway management, raising operational safety standards on the Carajás Railroad (EFC) and the Vitória to Minas Railroad (EFVM).

Vale is advancing its innovation and logistics efficiency strategy by adopting an advanced operational safety system for its rail transport. The company announced an agreement with Wabtec (NYSE:WAB) to implement the Positive Train Control (PTC) solution in railway management, raising operational safety standards on the Carajás Railroad (EFC) and the Vitória to Minas Railroad (EFVM).
The PTC system increases predictability and reliability in railway operations through advanced data transmission and monitoring technology. This solution enables real-time management of operations, automatic intervention in risk conditions, and mitigation of critical operational events. The project, with an investment of approximately R$1 billion, will be implemented in phases through 2031 and includes integration with onboard systems and existing infrastructure, ensuring an efficient and safe transition to the new operational standard.

The Vitória to Minas Railroad and the Carajás Railroad, operated by Vale, are already among the safest railways in Brazil, according to ANTT (Brazil's National Land Transport Agency) criteria, and are the only two regular passenger train lines in the country.

"The continuous strengthening of our safety culture and operational excellence is one of the pillars of Vale's future strategy. The adoption of this cutting-edge technology for railway management reinforces our commitment to using innovation as a lever for an increasingly safe, modern, and efficient operation across our integrated logistics chain," says Carlos Medeiros, Vale's Executive Vice President of Operations.

"The implementation of PTC in Vale's operations represents a significant milestone for the advancement of railway safety in Brazil. This project reinforces our commitment to purposeful innovation, driving digital transformation in railways and contributing to safer, more efficient operations," says Danilo Miyasato, President and Regional Leader of Wabtec LATAM.

The technology to be implemented will be Wabtec's I-ETMS (Interoperable Electronic Train Management System), developed by Wabtec and widely recognized in the global market as a benchmark for PTC systems in world-class asset operations.

About Vale
Vale is a global mining company that exists to improve life and transform the future together. Headquartered in Brazil and operating around the world, it is one of the largest global producers of iron ore, copper, and nickel. Its operations include extensive logistics systems integrated with its mines, including railways, maritime terminals, and ports. Vale's ambition is to lead value generation in mining ethically and sustainably. The company also aims to be a leader in steelmaking decarbonization, with competitive iron ore costs, a customer focus and adaptable portfolio, while accelerating growth in copper and increasing operational efficiency in nickel.

About Wabtec
Wabtec Corporation is revolutionizing the way the world moves for future generations. The company is a global leader in providing equipment, systems, digital solutions, and value-added services for the freight and transit rail industries, as well as the mining, marine, and industrial markets. For 155 years, Wabtec has led the rail industry and envisions contributing to a more efficient rail system in the United States and around the world. Visit Wabtec's website at www.wabteccorp.com.

en.title: Vale Celebrates Mariana's Anniversary with Immersive Experience and Free Cultural Programming
en.subtitle: Free events on July 17–18 at Praça Gomes Freire celebrate the history and cultural heritage of Mariana, Minas Gerais
en.body:
The public will be able to take part in an immersive experience through the municipality's cultural 
and historical heritage sites. Credit: Otávio Honoratto


As part of the celebrations for Mariana's 330th anniversary, Vale is promoting a special program at Praça Gomes Freire on July 17 and 18, featuring free activities for the public focused on celebrating the city's culture, memory, and historical heritage. On Friday (17th), activities run from 4 PM to 10 PM, and on Saturday (18th), from 10 AM to 6 PM.

The initiative reinforces the company's commitment to preserving Mariana's identity and invites residents and visitors to learn about projects and actions developed in partnership with the community.

The highlight of the program is the "Our Heritage" Immersive Experience, a sensory journey that celebrates the history, culture, and heritage assets of the municipality. The experience offers content that complements the "Our Heritage" web series and reveals unique aspects of Mariana's historical and cultural legacy.
 


Credit: Otávio Honoratto


Visitors will also be able to tour the Dam Decharacterization Program booth, where they can access information about ongoing projects and their progress, including the distribution of social giveaways.

The event will also feature a fair showcasing local producers, associations, and projects supported by Vale — a space dedicated to promoting the work of partner institutions that contribute to the social, cultural, and economic development of the region.

Visitors can also register to tour the company's local operations and learn more about the "Our Heritage" web series, a production that highlights initiatives dedicated to preserving the municipality's historical and cultural heritage.

"Our Heritage" Web Series
Launched by Vale, the "Our Heritage" web series presents stories, people, and initiatives that help preserve Mariana's rich historical and cultural heritage.

Across four episodes, the production highlights iconic sites in the city, such as the Mariana Museum, the School of Traditional Crafts, the Church of São Francisco de Assis, and the Mariana Railway Station, always through the perspective of the people who keep the memory and relevance of this heritage alive for the community.

Watch the episodes at www.vale.com/mariana

Informacion:
"Our Heritage" Immersive Experience and Cultural Programming

When:
July 17 (Friday) – 4 PM to 10 PM
July 18 (Saturday) – 10 AM to 6 PM

Location: Praça Gomes Freire, Mariana (MG)
Free admission

en.title: Preserving Tradition, Creating Opportunities: PT Vale-Supported MSME Products Showcased at the 2026 National PKK Movement Day and Dekranas Anniversary
en.subtitle: PT Vale once again demonstrated its commitment to supporting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) while preserving local culture through its participation in the 54th National Family Welfare Movement Day (HKG PKK) and the 46th Anniversary of the National Crafts Council (Dekranas) held in Makassar. During the exhibition at Trans Studio Mall Makassar from July 9–11, 2026, PT Vale showcased a range of products from its assisted MSMEs, including Teduhu woven crafts from Nuha Village and Sampa Konao crafts from Matano Village.
en.body:
PT Vale once again demonstrated its commitment to supporting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) while preserving local culture through its participation in the 54th National Family Welfare Movement Day (HKG PKK) and the 46th Anniversary of the National Crafts Council (Dekranas) held in Makassar. During the exhibition at Trans Studio Mall Makassar from July 9–11, 2026, PT Vale showcased a range of products from its assisted MSMEs, including Teduhu woven crafts from Nuha Village and Sampa Konao crafts from Matano Village.

This participation reflects PT Vale’s commitment to promoting community economic independence while introducing the cultural richness of East Luwu to a broader audience.

According to Endra Kusuma, Head of External Relations Regional and Growth at PT Vale, national events such as HKG PKK and the Dekranas Anniversary provide valuable opportunities for assisted MSMEs to expand their market reach and enhance their competitiveness.

“We want the communities we support to become more economically independent, build sustainable businesses, and gain greater recognition for their products—not only at the regional level but also nationally,” said Endra.

PT Vale’s support for MSMEs goes beyond product promotion. Through its Community Development and Empowerment Program (PPM), the company provides comprehensive assistance ranging from business infrastructure support and business management training to marketing, product development, and branding strategies. These programs involve experienced trainers and experts who help entrepreneurs improve product quality and strengthen their competitiveness.

In addition, PT Vale continues to create promotional opportunities through participation in various exhibitions, including events organized in collaboration with Indonesia’s Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM). The company also operates an MSME Gallery, serving as a permanent showcase for products developed by its assisted enterprises.

One of the standout products featured at the exhibition was Teduhu weaving, a traditional craft that carries significant cultural value but faces challenges related to the declining number of artisans.

“There used to be many artisans practicing this craft, but their numbers have decreased as fewer young people are interested in learning it. That is why we provide training for younger generations to ensure these skills remain alive and are not lost,” Endra explained.

These efforts have begun to yield positive results. Several assisted MSMEs have participated in provincial and national-level exhibitions, including events in Jakarta. Today, around five to ten assisted MSMEs have successfully expanded their market reach across the province, with the food and beverage sector continuing to be the largest contributor.

To further promote local products, PT Vale also utilizes products made by its assisted MSMEs as official souvenirs for guests and business partners. This initiative is expected to increase product exposure while opening up new market opportunities for MSME entrepreneurs in East Luwu.

Beyond supporting the exhibition, PT Vale also participated in the “Jalan Sehat Anti Mager” (Anti-Sedentary Healthy Walk) held on Saturday, July 11, as part of the 2026 National HKG PKK and Dekranas Anniversary celebrations. The company’s involvement reflects its commitment to strengthening collaboration with various stakeholders to support community empowerment, cultural preservation, and inclusive economic growth.

id.title: Melestarikan Tradisi, Membuka Peluang: Produk UMKM Binaan PTVI Tampil di HKG PKK Nasional dan HUT Dekranas 2026
id.subtitle: PT Vale kembali mendukung pengembangan UMKM sekaligus pelestarian budaya lokal melalui partisipasinya dalam Hari Kesatuan Gerak (HKG) PKK Nasional ke-54 dan Hari Ulang Tahun (HUT) Dekranas ke-46 yang digelar di Makassar. Selama pameran pada 9–11 Juli 2026 di Trans Studio Mall Makassar, PT Vale memperkenalkan berbagai produk unggulan dari UMKM binaan, termasuk anyaman Teduhu dari Desa Nuha dan Sampa Konao dari Desa Matano.
id.body:
PT Vale kembali mendukung pengembangan UMKM sekaligus pelestarian budaya lokal melalui partisipasinya dalam Hari Kesatuan Gerak (HKG) PKK Nasional ke-54 dan Hari Ulang Tahun (HUT) Dekranas ke-46 yang digelar di Makassar. Selama pameran pada 9–11 Juli 2026 di Trans Studio Mall Makassar, PT Vale memperkenalkan berbagai produk unggulan dari UMKM binaan, termasuk anyaman Teduhu dari Desa Nuha dan Sampa Konao dari Desa Matano.

Partisipasi ini menjadi bagian dari komitmen PT Vale dalam mendukung kemandirian ekonomi masyarakat sekaligus membantu memperkenalkan kekayaan budaya Luwu Timur ke khalayak yang lebih luas.

Menurut Head of External Relations Regional and Growth PT Vale, Endra Kusuma, ajang nasional seperti HKG PKK dan HUT Dekranas menjadi kesempatan penting bagi UMKM binaan untuk memperluas pasar dan meningkatkan daya saing.

"Kami ingin masyarakat binaan semakin mandiri secara ekonomi, memiliki usaha yang berkelanjutan, dan produk-produknya semakin dikenal, tidak hanya di tingkat daerah tetapi juga nasional," ujar Endra.


Dukungan PT Vale terhadap UMKM tidak berhenti pada promosi produk. Melalui Program Pengembangan dan Pemberdayaan Masyarakat (PPM), PT Vale juga memberikan pendampingan yang mencakup penyediaan sarana usaha, pelatihan manajemen bisnis, pemasaran, pengembangan produk, hingga strategi branding. Berbagai pelatihan tersebut menghadirkan narasumber berpengalaman untuk membantu para pelaku usaha meningkatkan kualitas dan daya saing produknya.

Selain itu, PT Vale terus membuka akses promosi melalui berbagai pameran, termasuk kegiatan bersama Kementerian ESDM, serta menghadirkan UMKM Gallery sebagai etalase permanen bagi produk-produk binaan.
Salah satu produk yang mendapat perhatian dalam pameran ini adalah anyaman Teduhu, yang memiliki nilai budaya tinggi sekaligus menghadapi tantangan regenerasi pengrajin.

"Dulu pengrajinnya cukup banyak, tetapi sekarang mulai berkurang karena generasi muda kurang tertarik. Karena itu kami mengadakan pelatihan bagi anak-anak muda agar keterampilan ini tetap hidup dan tidak hilang," jelas Endra.

Upaya tersebut mulai menunjukkan hasil positif. Beberapa UMKM binaan kini telah mengikuti berbagai pameran tingkat provinsi hingga nasional, termasuk di Jakarta. Saat ini, sekitar lima hingga sepuluh UMKM binaan telah berhasil memperluas jangkauan pemasaran mereka ke tingkat provinsi, dengan sektor makanan dan minuman masih menjadi penyumbang terbesar.

Untuk membantu memperkenalkan produk lokal lebih luas lagi, PT Vale juga memanfaatkan produk UMKM binaan sebagai suvenir bagi tamu dan mitra perusahaan. Langkah ini diharapkan dapat meningkatkan eksposur produk sekaligus membuka peluang pasar baru bagi pelaku UMKM di Luwu Timur.

Tak hanya mendukung pameran, PT Vale turut berpartisipasi dalam kegiatan Jalan Sehat Anti Mager yang menjadi bagian dari rangkaian HKG PKK Nasional dan HUT Dekranas 2026 pada Sabtu (11/7). Keterlibatan ini mencerminkan komitmen PT Vale dalam memperkuat kolaborasi dengan berbagai pemangku kepentingan untuk mendorong pemberdayaan masyarakat, pelestarian budaya, dan pertumbuhan ekonomi yang inklusif.

en.title: Vale Launches First-Ever R&D&I Report and Details How Innovation Is Already Transforming the Mining Chain
en.subtitle: With US$685 million invested and 45 AI solutions in use, Vale details how technology, automation and circularity are redefining mining
en.body:
Publication consolidates more than 350 projects and showcases applications of AI, automation, circularity, and decarbonization.
 


Vale has launched its first Research, Development & Innovation (R&D&I) Report, a publication that consolidates investments, governance, partnerships, and applied cases in the transformation of mining. More than just a compilation of technological initiatives, the report shows how R&D&I has become part of the company's strategy to address industry challenges such as operating more safely and efficiently, reducing environmental impacts, and expanding mining's contribution to the energy transition.

In 2025, Vale invested US$685 million (approximately R$3.78 billion) in R&D&I and maintained a portfolio of more than 350 projects. The agenda is supported by 16 proprietary innovation hubs and reinforces ties with academia, with more than R$38.4 million in scholarships linked to R&D&I projects developed at universities and research institutes, and more than R$10 million in research infrastructure.

The report starts from a central premise: the Mining of the Future will be defined by an entire chain transformed by science, data, automation, artificial intelligence, circularity, and lower-emission solutions. This chain begins with mineral research and exploration, moves through autonomous mines, digital plants, railways, ports, and shipping, and reaches steel industry clients with products and industrial models aimed at reducing emissions.

"Building the Mining of the Future requires discipline, continuous learning and the courage to innovate responsibly. The report shows that we are doing this consistently, integrating technical knowledge, field execution and a culture that always puts life first," says Paulo Celso Pires, Vale's Director of Technology and Innovation.

Artificial Intelligence in Practice: 45 Applied Solutions from Mine to Logistics
 


One of the report's highlights is the advance of artificial intelligence in industrial environments. Vale already has more than 45 AI solutions applied across its value chain, used in mining, plants, pelletizing, railways, ports, shipping, asset monitoring, mineral exploration, and corporate areas.

These technologies support decision-making and help solve concrete operational problems: forecasting weather conditions, supporting mining decisions, monitoring critical assets, optimizing maritime fleets, reducing input consumption, improving logistics predictability, and expanding safety. Examples include MinAInteligente, with AI applied to mine efficiency and predictability; SabIA, generative AI for searching technical mineral exploration information; PelotAInteligente, focused on optimizing pelletizing and reducing natural gas consumption; and VESO, a simulator that combines production, costs, and emissions to support decarbonization decisions.

Automation, Safety, and the Future of Work
 


The automation agenda reinforces that the Mining of the Future goes beyond technological evolution and also involves new skills, operating models, and ways of working. More than 90 autonomous pieces of equipment are operating in Brazil, including off-road trucks, drill rigs, and yard machines. The technology allows activities to be conducted from safer, more connected, and data-driven environments.
This movement is also linked to shaping the future workforce. Around 300 jobs have undergone transformation, with employees trained for new roles or to work differently, interacting with autonomous vehicles and machines.

 


Capanema Mine – MG. Credit: Nayara Leite


Among the most representative examples is the Capanema mine, in Ouro Preto, Minas Gerais, resumed after 22 years of inactivity. The operation was designed in line with the company's new paradigms: 100% autonomous operation, dry mining, no water use in processing, no tailings generation, no dams, and reuse of ore contained in a former waste rock pile.

Generating Value from What Has Already Been Mined
In 2025, Vale produced 26.3 million tonnes of iron ore from circular sources, equivalent to about 8% of total production — more than double what it produced the previous year. The goal is to reach 10% of annual production by 2030.
The Circular Mining Program brings together more than 100 initiatives, including the reuse of waste rock and tailings, sustainable sand production, the block factory at the Pico Mine, and solutions that turn materials previously treated as liabilities into new products or inputs for the production chain.

From Mine to Ship — and to the Customer
 


Innovation in mining also extends beyond the mine itself. In ports, railways, and shipping, Vale develops solutions aimed at safety, logistics efficiency, emissions reduction, and operational predictability. Initiatives include drones for ship mooring at Porto Norte (São Luís, MA), solar panels on Carajás Railroad locomotives, AIFleet, Ecoshipping, and VESO, a simulation tool that combines costs, production, and emissions.
In the steel chain, the company highlights products and solutions aimed at reducing customer emissions. Iron ore briquettes have the potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in steelmaking by up to 10%, while Mega Hubs can reduce emissions by up to 70% compared to the traditional route.


The full report can be accessed here.

en.title: Tax Reform: pay attention to new NF-e validation rules starting 08/03/2026
en.subtitle: New NF-e and NFC-e validation rules take effect on August 3, 2026; companies must adapt to avoid invoice rejection by SEFAZ.
en.body:
The Consumption Tax Reform is entering a new phase and requires attention from companies that issue Electronic Invoices (NF-e) and Consumer Electronic Invoices (NFC-e). Starting August 3, 2026, new validation rules related to the IBS (Tax on Goods and Services) and CBS (Contribution on Goods and Services) come into effect.

The change was published by the National NF-e Portal through Technical Note 2025.002 v1.50 and may directly impact invoicing, payments, and the continuity of the supply of materials and services.

What changes in practice?

Starting August 3, 2026, the fields related to IBS and CBS will become part of the NF-e and NFC-e validation rules.
This means that fiscal documents issued without these fields correctly filled in may be rejected by SEFAZ at the time of issuance.

What are the potential impacts?

When an invoice is rejected, invoicing is not completed. As a result, operational impacts may occur, such as:

  • Delay or inability to invoice;
  • Impact on receiving payments;
  • Delay in the delivery of materials;
  • Interruptions in service delivery until the situation is resolved.

For this reason, it is essential that companies prepare in advance to meet the new requirements.

How can your company prepare?

To avoid impacts on your operations, we recommend that suppliers:

  • Update or validate their invoicing systems (ERP);
  • Check that the IBS and CBS fields are correctly enabled for issuing NF-e and NFC-e;
  • Review their fiscal and tax parameterizations;
  • Run test issuances before the mandatory deadline;
  • Align adjustments with their Fiscal, Tax, and Accounting departments or specialized consultancies.

Mind the deadline

id.title: Tax Reform: pay attention to new NF-e validation rules starting 08/03/2026
id.subtitle: New NF-e and NFC-e validation rules take effect on August 3, 2026; companies must adapt to avoid invoice rejection by SEFAZ.
id.body:
The Consumption Tax Reform is entering a new phase and requires attention from companies that issue Electronic Invoices (NF-e) and Consumer Electronic Invoices (NFC-e). Starting August 3, 2026, new validation rules related to the IBS (Tax on Goods and Services) and CBS (Contribution on Goods and Services) come into effect.

The change was published by the National NF-e Portal through Technical Note 2025.002 v1.50 and may directly impact invoicing, payments, and the continuity of the supply of materials and services.

What changes in practice?

Starting August 3, 2026, the fields related to IBS and CBS will become part of the NF-e and NFC-e validation rules.
This means that fiscal documents issued without these fields correctly filled in may be rejected by SEFAZ at the time of issuance.

What are the potential impacts?

When an invoice is rejected, invoicing is not completed. As a result, operational impacts may occur, such as:

  • Delay or inability to invoice;
  • Impact on receiving payments;
  • Delay in the delivery of materials;
  • Interruptions in service delivery until the situation is resolved.

For this reason, it is essential that companies prepare in advance to meet the new requirements.

How can your company prepare?

To avoid impacts on your operations, we recommend that suppliers:

  • Update or validate their invoicing systems (ERP);
  • Check that the IBS and CBS fields are correctly enabled for issuing NF-e and NFC-e;
  • Review their fiscal and tax parameterizations;
  • Run test issuances before the mandatory deadline;
  • Align adjustments with their Fiscal, Tax, and Accounting departments or specialized consultancies.

Mind the deadline

Although validation will only be required as of August 3, 2026, now is the ideal time to make the necessary adjustments calmly and reduce business risks.
Companies under the Actual Profit (Lucro Real) and Presumed Profit (Lucro Presumido) tax regimes should prioritize their adaptation to ensure business continuity and avoid issues when issuing fiscal documents.

en.title: Inside Vale's Operations in Nova Lima: Beyond the Mines
en.subtitle: From around-the-clock environmental monitoring and 5,000+ hectares of preserved land to social projects and the Águas Claras Mine's sustainable future, a closer look at how Vale's presence shapes daily life in Nova Lima, Minas Gerais.
en.body:
Anyone who moves through Nova Lima knows that mining is part of the city's history, landscape, and daily routine. Yet the full extent of that presence is not always clear to residents. Looking only at the structures Vale maintains within the city, Nova Lima is home to 10 mining-related units: seven operational units, plus the Águas Claras Mine (which has ceased operations), the Ferrous Technology Center (CTF), and the Concórdia Building office.

Permanent Monitoring of Activities
One of the behind-the-scenes pillars of Vale's operations is environmental monitoring. At the Environmental Control Center (CCA), teams track environmental indicators around the clock in areas near the operations. The facility functions as a permanent observation room, designed to detect changes, support operational decisions, and track environment-related control measures.

Vale's mining presence in Nova Lima also coexists with an extensive conservation area. More than five thousand hectares of green spaces are preserved by Vale within the municipality, including legal reserves, environmental compensation areas, and Private Natural Heritage Reserves (RPPNs). Among these are the Mata do Jambreiro RPPN (912 hectares), the Serra da Calçada Natural Monument (527 hectares), and the Perdidas Natural Monument (289 hectares). For Jorge Falrene, Vale's manager of physical management of non-operational properties, these areas serve a purpose that goes beyond landscape preservation. "The preserved green areas help ensure shelter for fauna and flora and conserve water. In practice, this means greater environmental balance and better conditions for surrounding communities," he says.

Part of this preserved territory is now being opened to the public through the Vale Trail Circuit, developed in partnership with the Trilhas Project. The initiative plans 180 kilometers of registered trails that are being signposted and improved to broaden community access to preserved green areas.

Projects That Show Up in Neighborhoods
The mining company's impact also reaches communities through social, cultural, environmental, and sports projects. In Nova Lima, approximately 6,000 people benefit from initiatives supported by Vale. These include Teia do Bem, Espaço Social Transformar, and the Bola de Fogo Sports Association, which offer supplementary activities for children and teenagers — such as tutoring, ballet, judo, soccer, computer literacy, and music. Since 2024, Projeto Casa Oté in the Jardim Canadá neighborhood has also joined this group, focusing on strengthening 15 local social institutions through exchanges, training sessions, and mentorship. The list also includes the Cãomer, Asas, and Instituto Cresce projects, focused on awareness about animal care and environmental responsibility.

In Jardim Canadá, the benefits are visible in stories like that of Eduardo Fernandes Ribeiro Viana, a participant in the Bom de Bola, Bom na Escola program run by the Bola de Fogo Sports Association, supported by Vale. For him, the experience is a source of joy. "I feel happy when I take part in training sessions and championships with Bola de Fogo. I've been involved for four years and I love it," he says.

The Future of a Mine That Shaped the City's History
Among Vale's units in Nova Lima is the Águas Claras Mine (MAC), which ceased operations in 2002. Four years later, following the incorporation of MBR, Vale took over management of the territory and continued the mine closure process.
Since then, the area has undergone environmental recovery, geotechnical structure monitoring, and discussions about future uses. The MAC Future Use project aims to redefine the territory based on principles of environmental, social, and economic sustainability — with community participation and shared value creation between the company and society.

The goal is to transform the former mining area into a space for community life, conservation, and sustainable development. Of the MAC's more than 1,900 hectares, approximately 93% are expected to be designated for environmental conservation, protecting native ecosystems, fauna, flora, and water springs. In parallel, specific areas are receiving initiatives, partnerships, and projects that expand meaningful public access to the territory and contribute to shared value between the company and society.

This process is guided by the PAFEM — the Environmental Mine Closure Plan — which defines specific actions for each MAC structure, with a focus on stability, safety, and integration with the environment and the community. In May, the decharacterization works on dam B7A were completed. As a result of the interventions, the structure no longer accumulates water or sediment and therefore no longer functions as a dam.

According to Angélica Silva, Vale's General Manager of Geotechnics, the milestone reflects the progress of actions at the MAC. "The decharacterization of dam B7A at the MAC is another delivery that reinforces Vale's commitment to the safety of people and the environment," she highlights.

As part of the ongoing decharacterization of MAC structures, Vale has started construction work on dam B6, with completion expected in the second half of 2027. The works seek the same objectives as B7A — ensuring the structure ceases to function as a dam.

At the MAC, decharacterization works have already been completed on dam 8B and the auxiliary dike of dam 5. Structures 7B and 5 MAC are currently in the project development phase. Until all decharacterization works are completed, the dams remain subject to regular inspections and 24-hour monitoring by Vale's Geotechnical Monitoring Center (CMG).

en.title: Vale Música holds two special performances in Itabira featuring the Vale Música Youth Choir and Vale Música Youth Orchestra alongside Fernanda Takai
en.subtitle: Vale Música Youth Choir and Orchestra perform for free in Itabira alongside Fernanda Takai, celebrating Vale's 84th anniversary and the project's 25-year milestone
en.body:
Free programming takes place on June 26 and 27, in the month Vale celebrates 84 years in Itabira, the city where it was born.

In the month Vale completes 84 years in Itabira — the city where it was founded — Vale Música invites the community to experience two special moments of celebration, culture, and connection through music. On June 26 and 27, the project presents free performances featuring the Vale Música Youth Choir and the Vale Música Youth.
 

 
Orchestra alongside singer Fernanda Takai.
The program begins on June 26 with a performance by the Vale Música Youth Choir at the Teatro da Fundação Cultural Carlos Drummond de Andrade (FCCDA). Tickets are free and must be claimed in advance through Sympla. Organizers recommend that attendees arrive early, as tickets will only be valid until 15 minutes before the show begins. After that time, seats may be released to audiences present at the venue, subject to availability.

On June 27, the Vale Música Young Orchestra will perform at Praça do Areão, next to the bus terminal, in a special concert conducted by Lucas Anízio and featuring Fernanda Takai. Admission is free and open to the public. The performances are part of Vale Música's mission to democratize access to culture and provide high-quality artistic experiences for the community. In Itabira, the events also highlight the appreciation of cultural spaces and Vale's connection with the city through music. The program also celebrates the group's 25th anniversary.

The performances are part of Vale Música's mission to democratize access to culture and provide high-quality artistic experiences for the community. In Itabira, the events also reinforce the appreciation of cultural spaces and Vale's connection to the city through music. The program also marks the group's 25th anniversary.

Fernanda Takai joins the Vale Música Youth Orchestra in a performance that promises to move audiences with a specially curated repertoire for the occasion.


For conductor Lucas Anizio, more than a unique artistic moment, the concert represents the result of a process of musical education and human development carried out with students, while celebrating Bossa Nova. "Even with a larger orchestral ensemble, we sought to preserve the delicacy and fluidity of the genre, exploring nuances, dynamics, and timbres that bring the audience closer to the elegant and distinctly Brazilian atmosphere of Bossa Nova. The arrangements also celebrate the blend of popular tradition and symphonic sound, creating a bridge between different musical worlds," he said.

 

 
Both performances are an initiative and coordination of the Instituto Cultural Vale, sponsored by Vale through the Rouanet Law (Federal Culture Incentive Law). They are produced by Estação Conhecimento Serra and the Ministry of Culture.
 

 
Vale Música Youth Choir performs in three acts
Comprising 25 singers aged 16 to 26, the Vale Música Youth Choir is conducted by Max Michel Alves, who serves as the concert's musical director. The repertoire includes songs such as "Sobradinho," "Flor do Cerrado," and "Nada será como antes."

Date: June 26 – 8:00 PM | Venue: Teatro da Fundação Cultural Carlos Drummond de Andrade | Free tickets via Sympla — available from Tuesday (June 23) at: vale.com/itabira | Note: tickets valid until 15 minutes before the show | Initiative & coordination: Instituto Cultural Vale | Sponsorship: Vale, through the Rouanet Law

Vale Música Youth Orchestra and social development
One of the reference groups of the Vale Música Espírito Santo Project, the Vale Música Youth Orchestra will present the concert with 40 members. All musicians are public school students between the ages of 13 and 28. According to the conductor, arrangements by Gilson Peranzzetta, Gilson Santos, and Bruno Santos will enrich the show with a symphonic perspective on Bossa Nova.

Vale Música Young Orchestra Service + Fernanda Takai
Date: June 27 – 8 PM
Venue: Praça do Areão
Free admission
More information: vale.com/Itabira

en.title: Fostering Harmonious Industrial Relations, PT Vale Collaborates with South Sulawesi Ministry of Manpower and East Luwu Manpower Office to Conduct Training for Labor Unions
en.subtitle: Amid evolving regulatory dynamics and the growing need for alignment between employees and the company, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) reaffirms its commitment to maintaining a harmonious working environment. One of the company’s key initiatives is the Industrial Relations and Labor Training held at Taman Antar Bangsa (TAB).
en.body:
Sorowako, June 17, 2026 – Amid evolving regulatory dynamics and the growing need for alignment between employees and the company, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PT Vale) reaffirms its commitment to maintaining a harmonious working environment. One of the company’s key initiatives is the Industrial Relations and Labor Training held at Taman Antar Bangsa (TAB).

The program was conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Manpower, the South Sulawesi Provincial Manpower Office, and the East Luwu Manpower Office. Participants included representatives and union leaders from several organizations, including the Chemical, Energy, Mining, Oil and Gas, and General Workers Union (SPKEKP), Vale Indonesia United Workers Union (SPBVI), Mining and Energy Federation – Confederation of All Indonesian Trade Unions (FPE KSBSI), Indonesian Workers Struggle Federation (FSPBI), Vale Indonesia Staff Union (SSVI), and the Indonesian Prosperous Labor Union (PK SBSI).

  

PT Vale’s Senior Industrial Relations Analyst, Muhammad Parawansa Lamude, explained that the two-day training program is mandated under the Collective Labor Agreement (CLA), which requires the company to provide training for union and labor organization representatives.

“At PT Vale, labor unions are strategic partners in achieving sustainable business growth. This training reflects our proactive efforts to build a shared understanding among the company, employees, and the government, enabling us to jointly ensure a safe, productive, and harmonious working environment across all operational areas,” said Parawansa.

The initiative also received appreciation from Nasrullah, Industrial Relations Mediator at the East Luwu Manpower Office, who emphasized that such programs strengthen the tripartite relationship among employers, workers, and the government as an integrated system. He highlighted the importance of continued intensive collaboration to ensure sustained synergy among all stakeholders in the future.

  

In addition, the training aligns with the fundamental objectives of industrial relations: to foster harmonious, dynamic, and fair working relationships, covering aspects such as working hours, rest periods, wages, and labor protection.

“We highly appreciate initiatives like this. As a regulator in the labor sector, the government must remain responsive to the various workforce dynamics experienced by both employees and employers,” Nasrullah added.

Moving forward, PT Vale will continue to promote and initiate collaborative platforms as part of its commitment to sustaining business continuity while ensuring compliance with regulations and the protection of workers’ rights.

id.title: Wujudkan Hubungan Industrial Harmonis, PT Vale Kolaborasi Kemnaker Sulsel dan Disnaker Lutim Gelar Pelatihan Bagi Serikat Pekerja
id.subtitle: Di tengah dinamika regulasi yang dinamis serta tuntutan keselarasan antara pekerja dan perusahaan, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PTVI) berkomitmen untuk menjaga harmonisasi lingkungan kerja. Salah satu upaya yang dilakukan melalui pelaksanaan Pelatihan Hubungan Industrial dan Ketenagakerjaan yang berlangsung di Taman Antar Bangsa (TAB).
id.body:
Sorowako, 17 Juni 2026 - Di tengah dinamika regulasi yang dinamis serta tuntutan keselarasan antara pekerja dan perusahaan, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (PTVI) berkomitmen untuk menjaga harmonisasi lingkungan kerja. Salah satu upaya yang dilakukan melalui pelaksanaan Pelatihan Hubungan Industrial dan Ketenagakerjaan yang berlangsung di Taman Antar Bangsa (TAB).

Kegiatan tersebut berkolaborasi dengan Kementerian Ketenagakerjaan, Dinas Tenaga Kerja Provinsi Sulawesi Selatan, dan Dinas Tenaga Kerja Luwu Timur serta menghadirkan peserta yang merupakan pengurus dari Serikat Pekerja Kimia, Energi, Pertambangan, Minyak Gas Bumi dan Umum (SPKEKP), Serikat Pekerja Bersatu Vale Indonesia (SPBVI), Federasi Pertambangan dan Energi, Konfederasi Serikat Buruh Seluruh Indonesi (FPE KSBSI), Federasi Serikat Perjuangan Buruh Indonesia (FSPBI), Serikat Pekerja Bersatu Vale Indonesia (SPBVI), Serikat Staff Vale Indonesia (SSVI), dan Serikat Buruh Sejahtera Indonesi (PK SBSI).

Senior Industrial Relations Analyst PTVI, Muhammad Parawansa Lamude mengungkapkan, pelatihan yang berlangsung selama dua hari ini termaktub dalam Perjanjian Kerja Bersama (PKB) yang mengamanatkan perusahaan untuk melaksanakan training bagi pengurus serikat pekerja maupun serikat buruh.

  

"Bagi PT Vale, Serikat Pekerja dan Serikat Buruh adalah mitra strategis dalam mencapai pertumbuhan bisnis yang berkelanjutan. Pelatihan ini adalah langkah proaktif kami untuk membangun kesamaan persepsi antara perusahaan, pekerja, dan pemerintah sehingga dapat bersama-sama memastikan lingkungan kerja di seluruh area operasional tetap aman, produktif, serta harmonis," ungkap Parawansa.

Apresiasi atas pelaksanaan Pelatihan Hubungan Industrial dan Ketenagakerjaan ini disampaikan oleh Mediator Hubungan Industrial Dinas Tenaga Kerja Kabupaten Luwu Timur, Nasrullah yang menegaskan bahwa agenda seperti ini memperkuat hubungan tripartit antara pengusaha, pekerja, dan pemerintah sebagai satu sistem yang tidak terpisahkan. Kolaborasi intensif sangat diharapkan agar semua pihak dapat terus bersinergi dalam banyak hal di masa depan.

  

Selain itu, pelatihan ini juga sejalan dengan tujuan utama hubungan industrial, yaitu menciptakan hubungan yang harmonis, dinamis, dan berkeadilan terkait waktu kerja, waktu istirahat, upah, hingga perlindungan ketenagakerjaan.

"Kami apresiasi kegiatan seperti ini karena kami memahami bersama bahwa pemerintah sebagai regulator di bidang ketenagakerjaan harus responsif terhadap berbagai dinamika keternagakerjaan uang dialami oleh pekerja ataupun perusahaan," ujar Nasrullah.

Ke depan, PTVI akan terus mendorong dan menginisiasi ruang kolaboratif sebagai upaya untuk menjaga keberlangsungan bisnis yang berjalan beriringan dengan regulasi dan hak-hak pekerja.

en.title: Vale Reinforces Pioneering Approach in New ISSB-Standard Report, Highlighting Circular Economy as a Business Opportunity
en.subtitle: For the first time, Vale recognizes circular mining as a business opportunity in its ISSB-aligned report, expanding risk analysis to cover tailings dams, environmental licensing, community relations, and health and safety.
en.body:
Vale released on Monday (June 15), on a voluntary basis, its 2025 Sustainability-Related Financial Information Report, reinforcing the pioneering spirit and transparency of its management. For the first time, the company includes circular mining as a business opportunity in the document, recognizing sustainability's potential to generate value for the business.

Vale was the first mining company in the world and the first Brazilian company to publish, as early as last year, a report following the new standard established by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) for companies to disclose sustainability-related risks and opportunities.

The first edition focused in depth on climate-related data. In the second edition, Vale expands its risk analysis to four additional topics: tailings dams, environmental licensing, community relations and human rights, and health and safety — while also introducing a new business opportunity linked to waste reuse.

en.title: Maravilhas III Dam: May 2026 Updates
en.subtitle: Maravilhas III Dam reports stability in May 2026 as second-phase construction progresses under Vale's continuous monitoring
en.body:
The Maravilhas III Dam, located in Nova Lima, Minas Gerais, maintained adequate conservation status in May 2026, with a positive Stability Condition Declaration (SCD) and no active alert or emergency level on the structure.

Geotechnical Performance in May 2026
The Geotechnical Performance Assessment Report for May 2026 was prepared by the Engineer of Record (EoR), an external company contracted by Vale for independent structural evaluation. The document indicates that, based on data obtained through continuous monitoring and periodic visual inspections, the dam is performing within normal parameters. Geotechnical instruments are operating within expected parameters according to the hydrological cycle, and the safety factors obtained in stability analyses meet the minimum requirements established by current legislation.

Second-Phase Construction Works Resumed
In April 2026, the second-phase construction works on the Maravilhas III Dam embankment were resumed, with execution of compacted fill and installation of abutment contact drains. Activities continued throughout May. This phase represents the continuation of a project designed in two stages, using a downstream construction method. The safety of people, risk reduction, and environmental care are absolute priorities during all phases of the works.

Continuous Monitoring
The Maravilhas III Dam is monitored 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, by Vale's Geotechnical Monitoring Center (GMC). Monitoring combines automated geotechnical instrumentation with associated control levels and real-time structural visibility.

What Changed Compared to April 2026
In May, the activities initiated in April were maintained, with expanded access via the right abutment.

en.title: Vale Música Performs for the First Time in Governador Valadares with the "Arraiá Sinfônico" Show
en.subtitle: Free Symphonic Concert Celebrates Northeastern Brazilian Music in Governador Valadares
en.body:
The Vale Música Youth Orchestra will make its debut in Governador Valadares on June 20th, at 8:00 PM, at Teatro Atiaia, with the show "Arraiá Sinfônico" (Symphonic Hoedown). The free performance brings together symphonic arrangements inspired by Northeastern Brazilian music, paying tribute to the work of accordionist and composer Dominguinhos and other great names in Brazilian music, such as Alceu Valença, Geraldo Azevedo, and Zé Ramalho, among others.


Tickets will be available in two batches, opening on June 15th, with a second release on June 19th.


Under the baton of conductor Lucas Anizio, the concert revisits classics of Brazilian popular culture in a proposal that blends the sound of concert music with the strength and poetry of the Northeastern repertoire. Audiences will be able to hear iconic songs such as Anunciação, Lamento Sertanejo, Coração Bobo, and Chão de Giz, among other works celebrating the country's celebrated composers.

A total of 34 musicians will take the stage in Governador Valadares, in a special formation prepared for the performance.

"We selected songs with beautiful melodies and unforgettable lyrics from forró, xote, and baião, among other popular rhythms given a symphonic treatment through arrangements crafted especially for the show. Everything was planned with great care, and we hope the audience will cherish this moment," says conductor Lucas Anizio.

The show reinforces Vale Música Espírito Santo's mission to broaden access to musical education and promote world-class artistic experiences, bringing diverse audiences closer to instrumental and symphonic music.
Vale Música is an initiative of Instituto Cultural Vale, sponsored by Vale through the Rouanet Law (Federal Cultural Incentive Law). The event is produced by Estação Conhecimento Serra and the Ministry of Culture, with support from the Municipality of Governador Valadares.

Tickets: Free, available from June 15th (2nd batch on June 19th)

en.title: Vale opens model plant in Itabira with AI applied to operations and enhances safety and efficiency
en.subtitle: The Conceição 2 plant in Itabira, Brazil, now uses AI to monitor over 400 variables in real time, cutting unplanned shutdowns and reducing worker exposure to hazardous areas — and will serve as the blueprint for Vale's broader operational transformation.
en.body:
Pioneering initiative in iron ore production in Brazil integrates artificial intelligence into industrial processes, delivering gains in quality, sustainability, and competitiveness.
 



The municipality of Itabira, about 100 kilometers from Belo Horizonte (MG), where Vale was founded 84 years ago, has been chosen to host the company’s first high-tech plant, marking the beginning of a new operating model driven by data intelligence. The Conceição 2 plant has been modernized to integrate processes using Artificial Intelligence (AI), expand automation, and reduce people’s exposure to hazardous activities. With a capacity of 11.2 million tons per year, the unit will serve as a benchmark for expanding the model to other company operations.

  
“The model plant is more than a project: it represents a new way of operating, based on the application of advanced technologies that redefine standards of efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness in mining. This initiative positions Vale at the forefront of the most modern and innovative iron ore processing plants in the world. The Model Plant program integrates technologies and robust process governance, creating a safer, more predictable, and more efficient environment, with highly skilled people”, says Carlos Medeiros, Vale’s Vice President of Operations.

The initiative is part of Vale’s mining strategy for the future, based on more connected and sustainable operations, with technology and innovation as drivers of safety, efficiency, and value generation. The implementation of the Model Plant in Itabira took 1.5 years and included 51 solutions to eliminate bottlenecks and improve operations.

More than 100 monitoring cameras were installed across the plant complex, along with the automation of approximately 7,300 instruments, including new advanced measurement devices and sensors. Data intelligence is also used to control, manage, and optimize more than 400 variables across all stages of the ore processing workflow. Operating flows were also reviewed to anticipate failures and avoid unplanned shutdowns.

“The modernization of the new plant enables a more integrated, highly monitored, and safer operation. The system includes an artificial intelligence layer that supervises hundreds of variables and performs real-time adjustments to the production process according to the characteristics of the ore and the product,” adds Medeiros.


Results
 


In less than two years of the pilot project, the plant increased productivity by 25%, reaching its planned capacity. In 2024, production was 9 million tonnes (Mt), and for this year the plant is already capable of producing 11.2 Mt.
There was also progress in the plant’s product mix. The share of direct reduction pellet feed – a premium and strategic product for steel decarbonization—increased by 40%. In addition, mineral recovery was optimized, improving resource utilization and operational efficiency.

Quality gains include the application of online ore grade analysis technology during processing, enabling immediate adjustments. This technology allows instant correction of the mineral processing route, ensuring better use of the iron contained in the material and reducing waste generation. In 2026, the average iron content in waste was reduced by 26%.

Another important advancement is improved employee safety in the operational environment, with fewer manual interventions in the industrial plant. The implementation of new technologies includes remote operation solutions, such as robotic arms, and the automation of electrical and mechanical equipment, such as motors and valves, enabling the plant to be operated remotely from control rooms.

When access to facilities is required, real-time images and data support more precise planning of activities.
“The plant has reached a new level of digital maturity, with 100% of critical operational decisions supported by expert systems. This advancement combines innovation, technology, and technical expertise to increase efficiency, reduce impacts, and enhance predictability, with a focus on people,” says Rafael Bittar, Vale’s Technical Vice President.

The model also improves efficiency in the use of natural resources by increasing water reuse rates. Currently, 92% of the water used in the Conceição 2 plant is recirculated. After filtration of the ore and waste—the final stages of processing—the water returns to the operation.

“The Model Plant embodies Vale’s vision of the future of mining and is a decisive step toward safer, more sustainable, and more competitive mining, prepared for the challenges of the coming decades,” explains Bittar.

Partner ecosystem
For the implementation of the Model Plant in Itabira and the expansion of the model to other operational units, Vale relies on a strategic alliance with ABB, a global leader in automation and electrification.

“The Model Plant Program demonstrates extraordinary vision by combining cutting-edge technology with safety and operational excellence. The initiative positions Vale at the forefront of global mining. We are proud to contribute our expertise in automation, electrification, and digitalization technologies to the sector,” says Fausto Almeida, ABB’s Mining Director for South America.

One of the program’s differentiators is the creation of a partner ecosystem focused on integrating technologies already adopted by Vale.

This strategy optimizes existing investments, reduces the need for new capital, and accelerates results. In this context, ABB acts as a technology integrator, ensuring interoperability between systems and suppliers.

Shaping the workforce of the future
 

 
The Model Plant Program connects operations, technology, and people development for the future of mining. All 122 operators, instrument technicians, and leaders at the Conceição 2 plant were trained to operate under the new model, totaling more than 2,800 hours of training.
Digital transformation expands operational capabilities, with professionals better prepared to work in integrated environments, analyze data, and support real-time decision-making. This is the case of Ivo Castro, 43, an Equipment and Plant Installations Operator at Vale for 17 years.

“Technology has added a lot. I didn’t have much knowledge of digital systems, and I improved my skills during the training. Today I work with more safety, information, and agility. Before, I was constantly in the field, checking installations and performing manual operations. Now I can monitor areas on my phone, in the palm of my hand. I only go to the field when needed”, says Castro.

Vale maintains ongoing training programs to prepare employees for industry challenges. These include immersive training with simulators and virtual reality that replicate real operating conditions, enabling safe learning aligned with new digital demands.

The initiative reinforces the company’s commitment to turning technological advancement into opportunities for development, growth, and upskilling for its employees.

en.title: Preserved green areas help protect natural resources and improve quality of life in communities
en.subtitle: Vale preserves over 8,000 hectares in Central Minas Gerais, advancing environmental conservation and well-being for local communities
en.body:
The green areas preserved by Vale in municipalities in the Central region of Minas Gerais have contributed to environmental conservation and to the quality of life of local communities. Together, the areas located in Congonhas, Belo Vale, Jeceaba, and Itabirito total more than 8,000 hectares of preserved land, including legal reserves, environmental compensation areas, and Private Natural Heritage Reserves (RPPNs).

In Itabirito alone, there are more than 5,600 hectares of preserved areas — the equivalent of more than 5,000 soccer fields. In Congonhas, the total reaches 1,455 hectares. Belo Vale has 593 preserved hectares, and Jeceaba accounts for 434 hectares of protected areas. 

 

These spaces help conserve springs, streams, and native vegetation, while also providing habitat for various species of fauna and flora. In practice, preservation helps protect the soil, improve water quality, and support climate balance in the region.

According to Jorge Falrene, manager of physical management of non-operational properties at Vale, preserving these areas is a way of caring for both the land and the people. "These areas help conserve water, prevent soil erosion, and provide shelter for fauna and flora. In practice, this means better water quality, environmental balance, and improved conditions for surrounding communities," he highlights.

 

 

Beyond environmental preservation, the areas also contribute to recreational activities, social interaction, and well-being, strengthening the relationship between communities and the environment and encouraging care for future generations.

id.title: Preserved green areas help protect natural resources and improve quality of life in communities
id.subtitle: Vale preserves over 8,000 hectares in Central Minas Gerais, advancing environmental conservation and well-being for local communities
id.body:
The green areas preserved by Vale in municipalities in the Central region of Minas Gerais have contributed to environmental conservation and to the quality of life of local communities. Together, the areas located in Congonhas, Belo Vale, Jeceaba, and Itabirito total more than 8,000 hectares of preserved land, including legal reserves, environmental compensation areas, and Private Natural Heritage Reserves (RPPNs).

In Itabirito alone, there are more than 5,600 hectares of preserved areas — the equivalent of more than 5,000 soccer fields. In Congonhas, the total reaches 1,455 hectares. Belo Vale has 593 preserved hectares, and Jeceaba accounts for 434 hectares of protected areas. 

 

These spaces help conserve springs, streams, and native vegetation, while also providing habitat for various species of fauna and flora. In practice, preservation helps protect the soil, improve water quality, and support climate balance in the region.

According to Jorge Falrene, manager of physical management of non-operational properties at Vale, preserving these areas is a way of caring for both the land and the people. "These areas help conserve water, prevent soil erosion, and provide shelter for fauna and flora. In practice, this means better water quality, environmental balance, and improved conditions for surrounding communities," he highlights.

 

 

Beyond environmental preservation, the areas also contribute to recreational activities, social interaction, and well-being, strengthening the relationship between communities and the environment and encouraging care for future generations.

en.title: Instituto Cultural Vale Launches Free Course on Lei Rouanet
en.subtitle: Free training helps cultural producers, artists, and managers navigate Brazil's main cultural incentive law — from SALIC registration to project execution and financial reporting
en.body:
Vale, through Instituto Cultural Vale, is launching on the 11th the online course "Training for Cultural Agents," offering free access, a downloadable manual, and a completion certificate. The program guides cultural producers, artists, and the general public on how to use the Lei Rouanet (Brazil's main cultural incentive law), from project development to financial accountability.

The content will be available at https://institutoculturalvale.org/. The launch will take place at Centro Cultural Vale Maranhão on the 11th, at 6 PM, featuring a performance by Bumba meu Boi da Fortaleza and the presence of representatives from the Ministry of Culture, Vale, and cultural producers.

"Vale understands culture as a driver of human, social, and economic development in the territories. By investing in the technical training of cultural agents, we reaffirm our commitment to strengthening the creative economy, democratizing access to cultural funding mechanisms in Brazil, and reinforcing cultural diversity," says Mariana Luz, Vale's Director of Private Social and Cultural Investment.

Classes Are Accompanied by a Free Manual
Across five modules, the course covers every stage of an incentivized cultural project in a practical, accessible way, focused on the day-to-day reality of cultural management. Topics include: proposal writing; registration on the SALIC platform (used by the Ministry of Culture to manage projects under Lei Rouanet); project execution; fundraising; legal obligations; institutional communication; and financial reporting.

The launch marks the culmination of an in-person training cycle that visited 8 cities and trained more than 350 people. Developed by Suellen Moreira and Daniele Torres — professionals with a combined 40+ years of experience in the cultural sector — the course is complemented by the digital manual "Lei Rouanet: From Project Development to Financial Accountability," available for free download on the Instituto Cultural Vale website.

Vale holds the top position in the ranking of companies that most invested resources through federal cultural incentive laws in Brazil between 2020 and 2025. To strengthen its role in Culture, Vale created Instituto Cultural Vale in 2020, which has since supported more than 1,000 projects across the country, with an investment of over BRL 1 billion in Vale's own resources and through Lei Rouanet. Among these are a network of cultural spaces with free admission, each with a unique identity and vocation: Memorial Minas Gerais Vale (MG), Museu Vale (ES), Centro Cultural Vale Maranhão (MA), and Casa da Cultura de Canaã dos Carajás (PA).

Learn more at vale.com.

en.title: Vale Música performs for the first time in Governador Valadares with the show Arraiá Sinfônico
en.subtitle: Orquestra Jovem Vale Música makes its Governador Valadares debut with a symphonic tribute to Northeastern Brazilian music and Dominguinhos.
en.body:
The Orquestra Jovem Vale Música will make its first performance in Governador Valadares on June 20th, at 8 PM, at Teatro Atiaia, with the show "Arraiá Sinfônico". The performance brings together symphonic arrangements inspired by Northeastern Brazilian music and pays tribute to the work of accordionist and composer Dominguinhos, and other great names of Brazilian music, such as Alceu Valença, Geraldo Azevedo, Zé Maralho, among others.

Tickets will be available in two batches, opening on June 15th and a new batch on June 19th.
Under the baton of conductor Lucas Anizio, the concert revisits classics of Brazilian popular culture in a proposal that unites the sound of concert music with the strength and poetry of the Northeastern repertoire. On the program, the audience will be able to hear remarkable songs such as Anunciação, Lamento Sertanejo, Coração Bobo and Chão de Giz, among other works that celebrate renowned composers of the country.

 
"We selected songs with beautiful melodies and unforgettable lyrics within forró, xote and baião, among other popular rhythms that received a symphonic treatment through arrangements specially prepared for the show. Everything was thought out with great care and we hope the audience appreciates this moment", says conductor Lucas Anizio.

In total, 34 musicians will be on stage in Governador Valadares, in a special formation prepared for the performance. The show reinforces Vale Música Espírito Santo's proposal to expand access to music education and promote artistic experiences of excellence, bringing different audiences closer to instrumental and symphonic music.

Arraiá Sinfônico is an initiative and articulation of Instituto Cultural Vale, sponsored by Vale, through the Lei Rouanet (Federal Law of Cultural Incentive). It is produced by Estação Conhecimento Serra and the Ministry of Culture. The event has the support of the Municipal Government of Governador Valadares.
Service

Orquestra Jovem Vale Música – Arraiá Sinfônico
Date: June 20th
Time: 8 PM
Venue: Teatro Atiaia, Governador Valadares. Address: R. Mal. Floriano, 513 - Centro, Gov. Valadares
Tickets: available from June 15th, with second batch on the 19th


REPERTOIRE
1- Tenho Sede (Dominguinho/Anastacia)
2- Aí que saudade d'oce (Vital Farias)
3- Onde está você (Zezum)
4- Coração Bobo (Alceu Valença)
5- Dona da minha cabeça (Geraldo Azevedo)
6- Dia Branco (Geraldo Azevedo/Renato Rocha)
7- Chão de Giz (Zé Ramalho)
8- Feira de Mangaio (Sivuca/Glorinha Gadêlha)
9- Lá belle de Jour (Alceu Valença)
10- Lamento Sertanejo (Dominguinhos/Gilberto Gil)
11- Anunciação/Moça bonita (Alceu Valença/Geraldo Azevedo e Capinan)
12- Suíte Centenária (Medley Luiz Gonzaga)

ABOUT VALE:
Vale believes that culture transforms lives. As the largest private supporter of Culture in Brazil, the company sponsors and fosters projects in partnerships that promote connections between people, initiatives and territories. Its commitment is to contribute to an increasingly accessible and plural culture, while working to strengthen the creative economy.
To strengthen its work in Culture, in 2020 Instituto Cultural Vale was created, which has already supported more than a thousand projects throughout the country, with an investment of more than R$ 1 billion in Vale's own resources and through the Federal Law of Cultural Incentive, the Lei Rouanet. Among them, a network of own cultural spaces, with free admission, unique identity and vocation: Memorial Minas Gerais Vale (MG), Museu Vale (ES), Centro Cultural Vale Maranhão (MA) and Casa da Cultura de Canaã dos Carajás (PA). Learn more about Vale at www.vale.com.

 
ABOUT THE VALE MÚSICA PROGRAM:
An original project of Instituto Cultural Vale, the Vale Música Program is a collaborative network of teaching and learning between students from music hubs in four states — Pará, Espírito Santo, Minas Gerais and Mato Grosso do Sul — and professionals from the country's largest orchestras. In total, it involves around 250 professionals and more than 1,000 students in exchanges, classes and artistic residencies. Partners of the Vale Música Program include Orquestra Sinfônica Brasileira (OSB), Orquestra Ouro Preto, Orquestra Filarmônica de Minas Gerais, Orquestra Sinfônica do Estado de São Paulo (Osesp) and Nova Orquestra, sponsored through the Federal Law of Cultural Incentive.

ABOUT THE VALE MÚSICA ES PROJECT:
An initiative and articulation of Instituto Cultural Vale, sponsored by Vale through the Federal Law of Cultural Incentive, and produced by Estação Conhecimento Serra and the Ministry of Culture, the Vale Música Espírito Santo Project serves 350 beneficiaries, aged 07 to 29, at the Cidade Continental hub, in Serra, and at Parque Botânico Vale, in Vitória. The project features several Reference Groups such as the Orquestra Jovem Vale Música, the Camerata Jovem Vale Música, the Vale Música Jazz Band, the Banda Sinfônica Vale Música, the Coral Infantojuvenil Vale Música and the Coral Jovem Vale Música, which perform at events in Greater Vitória and other regions of the country. Among the artists who have performed with Vale Música ES are Roberto Menescal, Fernanda Takai, Ivan Lins, Milton Nascimento, Alma Thomas, João Bosco, Hamilton de Holanda, Indiana Nomma and Gilson Peranzzetta. Vale Música ES students have toured Brazil and abroad, performing at Carnegie Hall in the United States, in Serbia, Japan and the United Arab Emirates.
